The TPP is not the first trade agreement to have Investor State Dispute Settlements (ISDS). In fact NAFTA has them, so we can see how they might work in the TPP.

  • Companies can sue if "Their law made me lose money", when in fact the company can ONLY sue if they lost money. If the company cannot prove they lost money they cannot sue.

  • The arbitrator panel (whom each parties pick half of) awards the chemical maker billions in damages that the U.S. Taxpayers have to pay. Well it's possible to get a large settlement but phrases like "have to" take on a different meaning when dealing with governments. If a country loses they can choose to pay their fine, or not; or fix the law, or don't. Chemical company 'x' doesn't have police to enforce that, their only option is to ask their own government to extract that amount with tariffs if their country doesn't care then they are shit out of luck. This actually happens, a lot. The US lost an online gambling dispute and is just choosing not to pay.

  • The ruling can't be challenged in US courts! That's kind of the whole point, if a country is discriminating against a foreign company why would you also let that country's court rule on it? Again the arbitration panel only decides if the country is discriminating it can't force changes.
